- When sentiment is low (≤0.3) and forecast is high, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.
- After a sharp price spike, model tends to overshoot — cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is rising (≥0.6) and forecast is below recent 7-day average, adjust upward by 2–5% to reflect bullish momentum.
- If forecast is consistently above true outcome over 5+ days, apply mean reversion: subtract 1–3% per day until convergence with recent 10-day average.
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is volatile (fluctuating ±0.25), reduce forecast volatility by 20–30% to avoid overfitting to noise.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.2) and price is falling, forecast should not dip below 10% below recent low — avoid “panic sell” traps.
